heroHeadline: Congreso CDMX Admits 80% Legislative Backlog as UNAM Applicants March on Rectoría, a Metro Line 2 Train Catches Fire, and Fiscalía Targets Tepito Gangs and Property Despojo
heroSubtitle: The Congreso CDMX's outgoing Mesa Directiva president Jesús Sesma acknowledged August 19 that only 409 of 1,963 initiatives (21%) have been approved this term, warning the stalled Programa General de Desarrollo is 'braking the economy.' On August 21, UNAM applicants marched on the Torre de Rectoría demanding the rector's resignation over irregularities in the 2026 online admissions exam affecting roughly 58,000 test-takers. Security operations intensified: SSC detained eight suspects — six identified as Unión Tepito members — in two Cuauhtémoc raids on August 24, and the Fiscalía CDMX secured eight disputed properties and returned six to their owners on August 25 in an operation naming Los Tanzanios, the Cártel de Tláhuac and Los Rodolfos as the capital's leading despojo cells. On infrastructure, a fallen umbrella sparked a short circuit and small fire aboard a Metro Line 2 train at the Taxqueña terminal on August 24, briefly evacuating the station with no injuries. Jefa de Gobierno Clara Brugada also launched the Pacto Digital CDMX on August 24, a strategy to curb children's screen time and advance a Digital Rights Law after citing that 98% of CDMX teens spend 5+ hours online daily.
footerNote: Data sourced from official CDMX government reports (Gobierno CDMX, SSC, SACMEX, SEMOVI, CAMe, CONAGUA, FGJ-CDMX, Congreso CDMX), INEGI, Fiscalía CDMX, NASA, La Jornada, El Universal, Proceso, Milenio, Infobae México, N+, El Financiero, El Sol de México, Excélsior, La Crónica de Hoy, La Razón, La Silla Rota, El Heraldo de México, Reuters, AP, Euronews, US News, and institutional analyses from UNAM, IMCO, México Evalúa, and the Institute for Economics and Peace (IEP).
